source.name: fn_GetCustomerTotal

assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL (may need to be created or changed to public)
The Orders table exists in the dbo schema with columns CustomerID and TotalAmount
TotalAmount column is numeric/decimal type compatible with SUM aggregation
Function marked as STABLE since it reads from database tables but doesn't modify data
Parameter prefixed with p_ and variable with v_ following PostgreSQL naming conventions
ISNULL converted to COALESCE which is the PostgreSQL equivalent

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or change to appropriate schema (typically 'public'). PostgreSQL is case-sensitive for quoted identifiers.
Confirm that DECIMAL(18,2) precision and scale meet business requirements. PostgreSQL DECIMAL is equivalent to NUMERIC.

compatibilityNotes.description: Marked as STABLE (reads database, doesn't modify). SQL Server has no direct equivalent to PostgreSQL's volatility categories, but this affects query optimization.
ISNULL converted to COALESCE. Both functions behave identically for this use case, returning 0 when SUM is NULL.
SQL Server's WITH SCHEMABINDING has no direct PostgreSQL equivalent. PostgreSQL functions reference objects by name at execution time.
Converted to PL/pgSQL (LANGUAGE plpgsql). This is the standard procedural language for PostgreSQL, equivalent to T-SQL.
